name: Ciudad Autónoma de Ceuta
summary_text: Ceuta, an autonomous city rather than a comunidad autónoma, has no regional LGTBI or gender-identity statute—a framework gap it shares with Melilla and Castilla y León, recorded in the national regional-law inventories as a gap case only. No incident evidence, no enforcement data, and no hate-offence figure separating Ceuta from the national aggregate was retrievable; this is a statute-book gap, explicitly not an incident finding. The city's distinctive religious-demographic composition (Muslim and Hindu minorities under their own autonomous arrangements) and the border-fence crossing environment create a document-and-presentation context different from the rest of Spain, adding modest friction for a visitor whose identity documents do not match presentation. National criminal law and the state-level police (Policía Nacional, Guardia Civil) still operate in Ceuta, so the enforcement floor is unchanged; unlike the Basque Country and Navarra, Ceuta has no regional equality office, LGTBI observatory, or own police force.

sources.claim_summary: FELGTBI+ September 2025 'Radiografía' report on LGTBI+ education policy across Spain's autonomous communities (University of Salamanca + FELGTBI+ authors); its comparative inventory of regional LGTBI legislation (Table 2) is the source used to place Ceuta and Melilla among the units with no regional LGTBI statute.

sources.title: Legislación LGTBI - Plan LGTBI
sources.claim_summary: Index page of Spain's autonomous-community LGTBI legislation; lists each comunidad's law and states expressly that Ceuta and Melilla have no regional LGTBI statutes of their own and must instead apply the national equality framework and central-government policies.
